finding.title: Windows component aliases bypass local-install archive rejection
finding.summary: The verifier compares raw POSIX components with candy-runtime/native before Windows extraction removes trailing dots. A ZIP containing product/candy-runtime./native/hypergraph-motif-cuda-incremental-scope6d-tranche1-alias/src/main.cu (or native.) passes the actual verifier with zero issues, then extracts into the prohibited local-install namespace on Windows. The producer excludes that canonical extracted path. This breaks the independently verified contamination policy, while the normal clean/populated producer archives remain identical.

severity.rationale: CWE-180 produces a concrete release-policy validation bypass under Windows extraction. It requires a crafted archive and a reviewer trusting verification before extraction; bounded source contamination is demonstrated. Major security impact is not evidenced, so High/Critical are unjustified.
severity.changeConditions: Reject noncanonical Windows aliases before applying policy (for example trailing-dot/space components), retain independent producer/verifier checks, and add actual Windows extraction negative regressions. Remediation is a proposed follow-up only; preserved product bytes are unchanged.

confidence.rationale: Two variants reproduced with actual current verifier API, CLI, and Windows extractall; canonical negative control rejects the payload. Candidate hashes match prior qualification.

taxonomy.category: Archive path canonicalization before policy validation

codeEvidence.label: Raw component equality precedes platform canonicalization
codeEvidence.explanation: Trailing-dot component aliases do not equal either canonical anchor but extract to them on Windows.

finding.rootCause: The local-install policy compares raw member components instead of rejecting aliases that the supported Windows extraction platform canonicalizes to those same components.
finding.remediation: Reject unsafe/noncanonical Windows path components before namespace matching; retain raw member checks and add independent injection plus actual Windows extraction regressions. Proposed follow-up only; no product edits made in this closure attempt.

counterEvidence: Fresh clean/populated producer archives remain byte-identical and contain no local installation state. The canonical injected path is rejected. The verifier never executes archive content, and the demonstration writes only synthetic source bytes inside a disposable extraction root. No RCE, secret leak or privilege escalation follows from the evidence.
validation.evidence: Two archives passed verification and extracted matching synthetic bytes into the reserved namespace. The canonical-name control failed verification, and the producer excluded the extracted files.
limitations: No execution, credential disclosure, native activation or privilege escalation demonstrated.
validation.method: Actual current Python API/CLI and Windows ZIP extraction

attackPath.dataflow: Attacker-controlled ZIP entry name product/candy-runtime./native/<reserved-prefix>alias/src/main.cu (or native.) -> orig_filename -> PurePosixPath -> raw-component equality check does not match -> issueCount=0 and verifier CLI exit 0 -> Windows zipfile.extractall strips trailing dot -> bytes written beneath canonical prohibited local-install namespace.
limitations: Fresh clean/populated producer archives remain byte-identical and contain no local installation state. The canonical injected path is rejected. The verifier never executes archive content, and the demonstration writes only synthetic source bytes inside a disposable extraction root. No RCE, secret leak or privilege escalation follows from the evidence.
preconditions: Attacker supplies/repackages ZIP bytes; reviewer trusts local verifier before Windows extraction.
attackPath.reachability: A release reviewer runs the actual local verifier CLI on a submitted or repacked archive and then extracts it on Windows. No account privilege beyond supplying archive bytes is needed. The direct producer does not generate this alias archive; activation of native code or disclosure of private files is not established.
attackPath.summary: CWE-180 produces a concrete release-policy validation bypass under Windows extraction. It requires a crafted archive and a reviewer trusting verification before extraction; bounded source contamination is demonstrated. Major security impact is not evidenced, so High/Critical are unjustified.

remediationTests: Both candy-runtime. and native. injected members must fail verifier API and CLI before extraction.
Retain byte-identical canonical clean/populated archives and production-native false-positive controls.

surfaces.label: scripts/package-portable-source.py
surfaces.riskArea: Anchored exclusions, deterministic contents and legitimate source preservation
surfaces.notes: Reviewed full producer. Added guard at 442-453 casefolds complete root components and reserves arbitrary/empty suffixes. Existing controls retain credentials/build/cache/root-artifacts exclusion, file symlink rejection, fixed metadata, REQUIRED_FILES and collision checks. Fresh real baseline-plus-four-overlay archives reproduce exact prior SHA256; no source member removed.

surfaces.label: scripts/verify-portable-archive.py
surfaces.notes: Reviewed full verifier. Raw backslashes, absolute/drive paths, parent traversal, case collisions, symlinks/special files, permissions and CRC negative tests pass. Confirmed Windows trailing-dot namespace alias bypass CWE-180, Low. Both alias variants accepted; actual Windows extraction writes prohibited namespace bytes and producer excludes resulting file. Canonical local-install contamination rejected.

surfaces.label: tests/candy-scope6e-package.test.mjs
surfaces.riskArea: Synthetic test isolation and regression adequacy
surfaces.notes: Explicitly reviewed untracked new file omitted by compact inventory. Temp-only synthetic fixtures, no real install inspection; independent injection covers local variants, empty suffix, case, directory entries, all existing forbidden categories, metadata and CRC. Fresh focused command and full 286/286 file suite pass. Existing corpus lacks the confirmed Windows trailing-dot variant; follow-up regression proposed in finding.
